name: Optimist Hub Payment Gateway with Moka United for WooCommerce
author: Optimist Hub

sections.description:
This plugin adds a Moka United virtual POS integration to your WooCommerce store, for merchants taking payments in Turkey.

It uses Moka United’s hosted payment page (Ortak Ödeme Sayfası / WebPos): the customer is redirected to Moka United to pay, so you can start taking cards without ever handling card data yourself.

The card number, expiry date and CVC code are therefore never entered on your site, never pass through your server and are never stored in your database. Your PCI-DSS scope stays at SAQ A.

How it works

  1. The customer selects “Moka United” at checkout. The plugin renders no card fields at all (has_fields = false) — only your description text.
  2. The plugin creates a payment session on Moka United’s WebPos service and redirects the customer to Moka United’s hosted payment page.
  3. The customer enters their card details, chooses an installment plan and completes 3D Secure entirely on Moka United’s page.
  4. Moka United returns the customer to your store with a signed result. The plugin verifies the signature, re-checks the amount and confirms the transaction server-to-server with Moka United before marking the order as paid.

Features

  • Redirect (hosted payment page) flow — no card data is ever collected by the store (PCI scope SAQ A)
  • 3D Secure authentication
  • Installments, including the interest/commission rates of the customer’s own card, shown on Moka United’s payment page
  • An installment table on the product page, so shoppers can see the monthly cost before they reach checkout
  • The card brand logos and per-installment totals are read live from your Moka United dealer account
  • Compatible with both the classic (shortcode) and the block-based checkout
  • High-Performance Order Storage (HPOS) compatible
  • Test mode, which points every request at the Moka United test environment so you can rehearse the full flow before going live
  • Transaction log screen
  • English source with a bundled Turkish (tr_TR) translation; the interface follows the site language

Requirements

  • WordPress 6.4 or higher
  • WooCommerce 8.0 or higher
  • PHP 7.4 or higher
  • A Moka United merchant account (dealer code, API username and password)
  • TLS 1.2 or higher

External services

This plugin connects to Moka United services in order to process payments. This section describes exactly what data is sent, to which service, for what purpose and when.

1. Moka United — Hosted Payment Page (payment session creation)

  • Service address: https://clientwebpos.mokaunited.com (test environment: https://clientwebpos.refmokaunited.com)
  • Endpoint: POST /Api/WebPos/CreateWebPosRequest
  • Data sent: payment amount and currency, order number, order description, buyer full name, buyer email address, buyer phone number (optional), buyer address, basket line items (product name, quantity, unit price), dealer code and API username
  • Purpose: to create a payment session and redirect the customer to Moka United’s secure hosted payment page
  • When: when the customer places the order and the payment is initiated
  • No card number, expiry date or CVC code is sent in this request. Those details are entered by the customer directly on Moka United’s own page, in the customer’s own browser.
  • Provider policies (Moka United) — terms of use: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/terms-of-use ; privacy policy: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/privacy-policy

2. Moka United — PaymentDealer services (transaction verification)

  • Service address: https://service.mokaunited.com (test environment: https://service.refmokaunited.com)
  • Endpoints: POST /PaymentDealer/GetDealerPaymentTrxDetailList (transaction verification)
  • Data sent: transaction code and order number for verification; dealer code, API username and password for authentication
  • Purpose: to confirm server-to-server that the payment actually succeeded
  • When: on the payment return (callback)
  • Provider policies (Moka United) — terms of use: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/terms-of-use ; privacy policy: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/privacy-policy

3. Moka United — dealer information

  • Service address: https://service.mokaunited.com (test environment: https://service.refmokaunited.com)
  • Endpoint: POST /Dealer/GetDealer
  • Data sent: dealer code and API username
  • Purpose: to validate the connection credentials
  • When: when the settings are saved
  • Provider policies (Moka United) — terms of use: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/terms-of-use ; privacy policy: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/privacy-policy

4. Moka United — card logo CDN

  • Service address: https://cdn.moka.com/Content/BankLogo/
  • Data sent: nothing by the plugin. The customer’s browser requests one PNG image per card family shown in the installment table (for example https://cdn.moka.com/Content/BankLogo/AXESS.png). As with any other image on a web page, that request carries the image URL, the visitor’s IP address and the browser’s referrer and user agent.
  • Purpose: to display the card family logo (Axess, Bonus, Maximum, …) beside that family’s rows in the installment table.
  • When: when a product page, or a page containing the [moka_taksit_tablosu] shortcode, renders the installment table. The image is fetched by the visitor’s browser, never by the store’s server.
  • This is a static asset host. No payment data, no personal data and no credentials are sent to it, and the table works without it: a card family whose logo is unavailable is shown with its name only.
  • Provider policies (Moka United) — terms of use: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/terms-of-use ; privacy policy: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/privacy-policy

When Test Mode is enabled, requests 2 and 3 are sent to the Moka United test environment (service.refmokaunited.com) instead, and request 1 is sent to the test WebPos address (clientwebpos.refmokaunited.com). The card logo CDN has no test counterpart; it is a static asset host. No request is made to Moka United at all while the gateway is disabled.

No card data is ever sent to any Moka United service by this plugin, and no card data is ever collected on your site. Card details travel from the customer’s browser directly to Moka United’s payment page. The plugin neither collects, nor transmits, nor stores them (PCI scope SAQ A).

The service provider is Moka United (Moka Ödeme Kuruluşu A.Ş.), not Optimist Hub. The terms of use and privacy policy of that provider are linked under each service above. Because this plugin uses Moka United’s payment service, the following also applies:

  • Moka United terms and conditions of payment services: https://www.mokaunited.com/legal-documents-and-representatives/terms-and-conditions-of-payment-services

This plugin contacts no other external service. It does not use its own update server; updates are delivered through WordPress.org.

Some further domains appear in the plugin’s code but are never contacted. They are listed here so the list above is exhaustive:

  • moka.com — the host allow-list used when validating a logo URL that the Moka API returned. It is a validation rule, not a connection; the only logo requests actually made are the cdn.moka.com images described in 4.
  • service.moka.com — the bundled Moka PHP client’s built-in default address. The plugin always sets the PaymentDealer address explicitly (see 2 and 3 above), so this default is never used.
  • service.refmoka.com — a retired test address. It appears only in a code comment recording that it no longer works; nothing calls it.
  • github.com — appears only in the file headers that the Strauss build tool writes into the bundled library, crediting itself. No request is made.
sections.installation:
1. Install and activate the plugin from your WordPress dashboard.
  2. Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Payments.
  3. Find Moka United, click Manage, enable it and enter the Dealer Code, API Username and API Password provided by Moka United.
  4. Leave Test Mode on until you have verified the payment flow, then turn it off to go live.
sections.faq:
Do I need a Moka United account?

Yes, for live payments. You need a Moka United merchant account and the dealer code, API username and API password issued to you. Moka United also issues a separate test account, which you can use with Test Mode to rehearse the whole flow — placing an order, paying on the hosted page and receiving the callback — without moving real money.

How do I enable test mode?

Go to WooCommerce → Settings → Payments → Moka United and tick Test Mode. While it is on, all requests go to the Moka United test environment. Remember to turn it off before going live: sending a test dealer to the live environment returns an InvalidAccount error.

How do I enable installments?

Installment options are rendered by Moka United on its own payment page. In the plugin settings you control whether installments are offered at all (Installment Options / “Taksit Seçenekleri”), the highest installment count to offer (Maximum Installment / “Maksimum Taksit”), and exactly which installment counts are listed (Installment List / “Taksit Listesi”, for example 1,2,3,6,9,12). Tick Reflect Commission in Installments / “Komisyonu Taksite Yansıt” if you want Moka United to apply the card BIN’s commission rates to the displayed installment amounts.

Are my customers’ card details safe?

They are never seen by your store. The card number, expiry date and CVC code are entered by the customer directly on Moka United’s page, which is operated by Moka United, not by this plugin. The plugin does not collect, transmit or store card data under any circumstance — not even in debug logs. This keeps your PCI-DSS scope at SAQ A.

Can I issue refunds?

Not from this plugin. Refunds are handled in the Moka United merchant panel
(https://pos.mokaunited.com). The plugin deliberately does not declare
WooCommerce refund support, so the refund button is hidden on the order
screen rather than offering an action that cannot complete.

How do I migrate from the old plugin?

The old moka-woocommerce plugin distributed through GitHub used the same gateway ID (mokapay), so your existing settings are inherited automatically. Before activating this plugin, deactivate the old one to avoid registering the same gateway twice. On upgrade, the plugin also purges any card data that the old version may have recorded in plain text, and removes a table the old version no longer uses. Take a database backup first.

Which languages are supported?

The plugin ships in English and includes a Turkish (tr_TR) translation, so a Turkish WordPress site shows the interface in Turkish and any other locale shows English. Every string is translatable, so additional languages can be added through translate.wordpress.org. If you want to ship your own translation, drop a .po/.mo pair into the plugin’s languages/ folder.

Which order status is assigned after payment?

You choose it in the plugin settings. The default is Completed.
sections.changelog:
1.1.8

  • Changed: the source strings are English, following the WordPress.org convention. The interface was Turkish-only before, which meant an English site also showed Turkish.
  • Added: a bundled Turkish (tr_TR) translation, so Turkish sites keep the Turkish interface. Every string is now translatable and additional languages can be contributed on translate.wordpress.org.

1.1.7

  • Changed: the plugin author is Optimist Hub again, linking to the https://profiles.wordpress.org/optimisthub/ profile.

1.1.6

  • Added: a screenshot of the installment table to the plugin page.

1.1.5

  • Fixed: the tag list had six entries; WordPress.org only keeps the first five and silently drops the rest, so one tag was being discarded without any warning. The list is now exactly five tags: woocommerce, payment gateway, moka, moka united, united payment. The “taksit” tag was removed.

1.1.4

  • Changed: the display name is now “Optimist Hub Payment Gateway with Moka United for WooCommerce” (the brand name is written in two words). The slug is unchanged.
  • Added: the “united payment” tag, so the plugin is found by the payment provider’s own name as well as by “moka united”.

1.1.3

  • Changed: the plugin author is now Fatih Toprak (https://profiles.wordpress.org/fatih-toprak/).
  • Added: screenshots to the plugin page.

1.1.2

  • Fixed: the payment method did not appear at all on the block checkout (“There are no payment methods available”). WooCommerce Blocks requires a canMakePayment property in the registration; without it the registry threw a TypeError and the method was never registered. The classic checkout was unaffected, which is why this went unnoticed.
  • Fixed: the currency is now sent to Moka. It was never sent, so Moka applied its own default (TL) — a store whose currency was not TRY would have had the right amount charged in the wrong currency. Moka accepts TL, USD, EUR, GBP, CHF, JPY, RUB, CAD, AUD, SAR, KWD, SEK, NOK and DKK; TRY is mapped to Moka’s own code TL.
  • Added: the gateway is no longer offered when the store currency is one Moka does not accept, and the settings screen explains why instead of letting the method disappear silently.
  • Fixed: the test-mode warning was printed twice on the block checkout.

1.1.1

  • Added: the Moka United card logo CDN (cdn.moka.com) to the “External services” section, together with what the visitor’s browser sends when it loads a logo.
  • Added: the public Moka United terms of use and privacy policy. The previous readme said no public terms page existed; that was wrong. The links are now listed under each individual service, as the review asks, and the payment services terms are linked as well.
  • Security: the payment callback is now sanitized on the same line its $_GET/$_POST values are read, so no raw request value can reach the callback handler or the payload stored as order_details. That stored payload is text-sanitized as well.
  • Fixed: the product tab escapes its output with wp_kses() and an explicit tag list instead of echoing it unescaped.
  • Fixed: the bundled Moka client no longer contains an unsanitized $_SERVER read.

1.1.0

  • Renamed: the plugin is now “OptimistHub Payment Gateway with Moka United for WooCommerce” and its slug is optimisthub-moka-united-payment-for-woocommerce, which is the text domain as well.
  • Fixed: a fatal error on PHP 7.4 when a card logo URL had to be checked against Moka’s CDN (str_ends_with() is PHP 8.0+). The same check now also rejects a bare .moka.com host.
  • Fixed: the installment table stylesheet is now loaded with wp_enqueue_style() instead of being printed into the page as an inline <style> block; the remaining inline style attributes moved into that stylesheet.
  • Security: the bundled Moka client now reads every $_SERVER value through a sanitising helper and validates the ClientIP it falls back to, so a request header can no longer carry an unvalidated value into a payment request. ClientPort is reduced to digits before use.
  • Security: sensitive-field redaction now has a second layer that works on the value, not only on the field name. Any value that looks like a card number (13-19 digits, Luhn-valid, with or without spaces or dashes) is replaced with [purged] whatever the field happens to be called, so the promise that card data never reaches a debug log or a database row no longer depends on knowing every field name in advance.
  • Added: the Requires Plugins: woocommerce header, so WordPress verifies WooCommerce is present before activation.
  • Changed: the bundled Moka client no longer uses cURL. Every request goes through the WordPress HTTP API (wp_remote_request()), which is the transport the plugin already injected at runtime.
  • Changed: Plugin URI now points at https://optimisthub.com/ (the previous URL returned 404).

1.0.1

  • Security: server-to-server verification now requires both PaymentStatus = 2 and TrxStatus = 1. Previously only TrxStatus was checked, so cancelled (3,1) and pre-authorised (1,1) transactions were treated as paid even though no money was captured.
  • Security: the API response gate is now fail-closed. A top-level ResultCode error is no longer accepted merely because Data.IsSuccessful is true — that flag means “the request was processed”, not “the payment succeeded”.

1.0.0

  • Initial release.
  • Redirect payment through the Moka United Hosted Payment Page (WebPos).
  • No card data collected, transmitted or stored — PCI scope SAQ A.
  • 3D Secure flow, installment display and commission handling managed on Moka United’s page.
  • Server-to-server transaction verification with signature and amount checks.
  • Classic and block-based checkout support.
  • HPOS compatibility.
  • Test mode.
  • Transaction log screen.
  • Automatic inheritance of settings from the previous moka-woocommerce plugin (gateway ID mokapay).

upgrade_notice.1.1.1: Second review round: external-service disclosure completed and callback input sanitized. No settings are lost.
upgrade_notice.1.1.0: Renamed plugin and slug, plus fixes for a PHP 7.4 fatal error in the installment table and for unvalidated request-header values in the bundled Moka client. No settings are lost.
upgrade_notice.1.0.1: Security update: cancelled and pre-authorised transactions could be treated as successful payments. Please update immediately.
upgrade_notice.1.0.0: Initial release. Deactivate the old moka-woocommerce plugin before activating this one. Back up your database first: the upgrade purges legacy card data and removes a table the old version no longer uses.
